summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with chest pain, nausea, vomiting, and hypertensive emergency. Initial evaluation ruled out acute coronary syndrome and pulmonary embolism, though EKG showed ST depressions and troponin was mildly elevated, consistent with her baseline due to ESRD. Blood pressure was controlled with IV nicardipine initially, then transitioned back to oral medications. She reported odynophagia, prompting GI and ENT consultation. Laryngoscopy suggested GERD, and EGD confirmed reflux esophagitis. She was started on high-dose pantoprazole, after which symptoms resolved. Leukocytosis, likely related to esophageal inflammation, improved without antibiotics. She remained stable throughout the stay, with controlled diabetes, continued dialysis, and no seizure activity. She was discharged to an extended care facility on pantoprazole 40 mg twice daily for eight weeks, with follow-up arranged with PCP and GI.
